Subject: Production: sudden latency and 5xx spike on private cluster

Karthik / Marissa —

We’re seeing a sustained p95 jump from ~180ms to 1.1s and an increase in 5xx errors starting at 07:30 PST across our VPC deployment (cluster oakridge-prod-1). The spike correlates with a batch of nightly ingest requests but persists for normal traffic as well. Attached are sampling logs and a heap snapshot; infra also forwarded a short trace.

Key customer impact:
- Frontend alerts showing degraded latency affecting the transaction approval flow (blocking checkouts)
- Error rate ~2.8% 5xx in the last 10 minutes

We need an ETA for mitigation and would like an executive sync in 30–45 minutes if possible. Please advise immediate runbook steps we can take (we can tolerate a short rollback window).

Attachments: perf-sample-logs-20261115.tar.gz, heap_snapshot_07-46.zip

Sienna Park

Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 08:10:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Production: sudden latency and 5xx spike on private cluster

Triage update (first-pass, attaching p95 profile):

Observations from sample logs + traces:
- There’s a sharp increase in KV cache miss rate starting 07:28 PST on shard 4; cache hit rate dropped from 86% -> 12% for prefix keys.
- Tokenizer CPU time per request increased ~3x for longer sequences — we see tokenization falling back to the slower path on ~30% of requests.
- A small subset (~4%) of requests show a decoder OOM fallback that results in 5xx. Heap snapshot indicates transient memory pressure coincident with inf requests.

Immediate mitigation options (ranked by risk):
1) Canary rollback to redwood-infer:2026.10.2 (previous stable) on one node pool to validate behavior (~10–12 min to roll).
2) Toggle prefix cache to aggressive warming mode (prefix_cache.warm=true) — low risk, immediate, may restore hit-rate for warm keys.
3) Temporary request-throttling rule for nightly ingest path (reduce concurrency) — medium impact to throughput but fast.
4) Switch offending queues to quantized 8-bitA runtime (quant-8bitA profile) to reduce memory pressure for decoder — requires hot swap on model variants (~20–30 min).

Recommended immediate action: do (2) + (3) now while we prepare a canary rollback (1) as guarded fallback. If we still see >1% 5xx after 15 minutes, escalate to canary rollback.

Attachments: p95-profiles-20261115.json

Marissa Cole
Customer Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sienna Park <sienna.park@oakridge.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 08:28:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Production: sudden latency and 5xx spike on private cluster

Ops note / escalation plan:

We’ve validated Marissa’s findings on our side. Additional infra notes: the runtime image redwood-infer:2026.10.4 included an attention-kernel reshuffle that altered KV allocation heuristics; this lines up with the cache thrash.

Planned actions (I will own execution):
- 08:35 PST: Apply prefix_cache.warm=true via the control plane on oakridge-prod-1 (low-risk).
- 08:40 PST: Throttle nightly-ingest route at the edge to 40% concurrency (config change lives in Redwood Console).
- 08:45 PST: If error rate >1.0% after the above, initiate canary rollback to redwood-infer:2026.10.2 on node pool alpha (expected 12–15 min).

Exec ask for LAURA / KARTHIK: Oakridge has requested an exec-level summary and a small customer credit request if rollback is required. We should prepare a one-page impact note and a credit recommendation in the bridge at 08:15.

I’m starting the prefix cache toggle now. I’ll post telemetry and incident link to PagerDuty.

— Jonas
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
